title: AuthZ entitlement bundles experiment & contract acceptance matrix
creator: Priya Shah
description: Objective: Define and validate a small set of enterprise-facing packaging bundles that make SSO, SAML assertions, and role-based access control (RBAC) contractual commitments explicit; measure commercial impact and sales friction. Scope: 1) Draft three candidate bundles (Base Enterprise, Security Add-on, Compliance Suite) with clear contract clauses and entitlements. 2) Produce a contract acceptance matrix mapping each entitlement (SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, data residency) to pricing uplift, SLA commitments, and legal obligations. 3) Run a lightweight field experiment with 6 targeted accounts via sales-assisted offers and track conversion and objections. Out-of-scope: major legal rework of master agreements, on-prem deployment technical changes (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Completed contract acceptance matrix (CSV/Confluence) that maps entitlement -> minimum contractual language -> pricing uplift band
A2: Three packaging SKUs documented with example clause language and T&Cs variations
A3: Sales playbook and objection handling notes for top 5 security questions
A4: Pilot executed with at least 4 accounts engaged and qualitative feedback captured
A5: Legal and Security sign-off obtained for template clauses (email thread or approval ticket)
success_metrics: Metric 1: Pilot conversion lift (trial->paid) >= 12% vs control
Metric 2: Average contracted ACV uplift for customers accepting Enterprise bundle >= $18k/year
Metric 3: Reduction in Security Questionnaire turnaround time for accepted template clauses <= 10 business days
Metric 4: Sales objection rate for auth-related clauses reduced by 35% after playbook rollout
